title: Delayed Formation of Landau Polaritons in Phase-Resolved THz Spectroscopy
authors: Noureddine Charrouj, Yurii Ivonyak, Dmitriy Yavorskiy, Vladimir Y. Umansky, Jerzy Lusakowski, Wojciech Knap, Marcin Bialek
abstract: Strong light-matter coupling gives rise to polaritons through coherent and periodic energy exchange between electromagnetic cavity fields and material excitations. While this interaction is typically inferred from spectral mode splitting, its dynamics remain largely unexplored. Here, using phase-resolved terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, we observe Rabi oscillations of Landau polaritons formed by coupling the cyclotron resonance in a GaAs/Al$_{0.36}$Ga$_{0.64}$As two-dimensional electron gas with Fabry-Perot cavity modes. By employing cross-polarized spectroscopy and magnetic-field differential, we resolve the temporal beating of the cyclotron resonance oscillations. Remarkably, we find that the Rabi oscillations do not start immediately after excitation of the cyclotron resonance, but after a delay corresponding to one cavity round-trip time. This demonstrates that the strong-coupling regime sets up only after the formation of the cavity mode field. Our results provide direct insight into the dynamics of hybrid light-matter states in the THz regime.
summary: The researchers used phase-resolved THz spectroscopy to study Landau polaritons formed by coupling cyclotron resonance in a 2DEG to a cavity. They found that the characteristic Rabi oscillations do not appear instantly upon excitation but are delayed until one full cavity round-trip time has elapsed. This result offers crucial dynamic insight, demonstrating that strong coupling is a process built up over time rather than an instantaneous effect.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamic formation and coherent energy exchange within Landau polaritons formed by strong light-matter coupling.
main_result: The Rabi oscillations of these polaritons are observed to be delayed, commencing only after a time delay corresponding to one cavity round-trip time. This proves that the strong-coupling regime is dynamically established through the evolution of the cavity field.
method: Phase-resolved terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) was employed, utilizing cross-polarized and magnetic-field differential measurements to resolve temporal beating.
model_or_system: The system involves coupling between the cyclotron resonance in a GaAs/Al0.36Ga0.64As two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) and confined Fabry-Perot cavity modes, forming Landau polaritons.
key_observables: Rabi oscillations (time beating), Faraday rotation angle spectra ($	heta_F$), and time-domain reflection signals ($R_x$, $R_y$).
important_parameters: Cavity period ($\sim 9$ ps for thick substrate); Rabi oscillation periods (e.g., $22$ ps observed).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on phase-sensitive THz measurements to resolve dynamics beyond simple envelope measurements.
figures_summary: Figures show time-domain traces of cross-polarized signals ($R_y$) exhibiting beating, and Faraday angle spectra ($	heta_F$ vs $B$) displaying zigzag patterns characteristic of strong coupling.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical system (2DEG coupled to a cavity), then using time-domain spectroscopy to observe Rabi oscillations, culminating in the key finding that these oscillations exhibit a measurable onset delay linked to the cavity round-trip time.
why_interesting: This work provides direct experimental evidence of the *dynamics* of strong light-matter coupling, moving beyond static spectral measurements. The observation of a build-up time scale is crucial for understanding open quantum systems where field buildup dictates coherence.
